newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cricket: Warne out of India tour, McIntyre called in.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cricket: Warne out of India tour, McIntyre called in.

text.p: Leg-spinner Shane Warne has withdrawn from the Australian team to tour India next month, the Australian Cricket Board (ACB) announced on Wednesday.

ACB chief executive Graham Halbish said in a statement that Warne, who underwent surgery on the fourth finger of his bowling hand in May, would not be fit to play in a test against India set to begin in New Delhi on October 10.
South Australia leg-spinner Peter McIntyre will take Warne's place in the 14-man Australia squad, Halbish said.
Halbish added the decision had been made after Warne had spoken to coach Geoff Marsh, captain Mark Taylor, team physiotherapist Errol Alcott and the national selectors.
"It was decided it was in Warne's best interests to withdraw when it became apparent he would be unable to play in the test match in New Delhi early next month," Halbish said.

"There was much consideration given to the thought that Shane should remain in the team environment for further treatment but, upon consultation with Errol Alcott, it was decided he should remain in Australia once it became apparent he would not be fit for the test match," he said.
Warne missed Australia's tour to Sri Lanka earlier this month for a limited overs series and has been training with his Victoria state side in Darwin this week.
Taylor on Wednesday confirmed he will lead the side on the six-week tour of India after making a successful recovery from back surgery.
